theory.summary: Premier Bach two-voice counterpoint study passing an agile 16th-note motif imitatively between both hands.
theory.pattern_tip: Track the 7-note ascending motif (C-D-E-F-D-E-C) and its upside-down inversion in Bars 3-4 as it modulates to G Major.
theory.technique_tip: Use crisp non-legato 8th notes against smooth legato 16ths so the two contrapuntal voices never blur.
theory.ballade_link: Trains complete two-hand independence essential for Chopin's inner-voice counterpoint.
concept_paragraphs: Bach's Invention No. 1 is pure musical architecture: virtually the entire opening eight bars grows out of one tiny seven-note motif (C-D-E-F-D-E-C), tossed back and forth between Right Hand and Left Hand in imitation.

Look closely at Bars 3-4: Bach flips that rising motif upside down (Inversion!) while climbing sequentially onto G Major via D7 (V7/V). Reading the motif shape makes intricate 16th-note counterpoint intuitive.

form_map.role: Subject exposition (RH answered 2 beats later by LH), pivoting via inverted sequence to G.
Imitative dialogue in G Major alternating C (IV/V) and D7 (V7/V) into a poised G cadence.

practice_steps: 1. Spot every entrance of the 7-note motif in both staves—circle them mentally before playing.
2. Play Hands Separately in Wait-for-Note so each hand learns its subject & countersubject cleanly.
3. Contrast crisp, detached 8th notes against smooth legato 16th-note motifs.
4. Combine Hands Together at 60% (46 BPM) before advancing to 76 BPM.
